input.rationale: The package guide permits same-batch entry persistence concurrent with messages, whereas Ready.Messages requires append before send. README also requires Entries before changed HardState; the experiment restricts the selected follower batch to unchanged HardState and persists every preceding batch. This is a conditional policy exploration at serialized RawNode entry, not an assertion that RawNode permits the early-send policy or that Node guidance overrides Ready. Actual election, leader self acknowledgment, follower response production and leader consumption occur within each independent run. MemoryStorage substitutes for disk durability and no crash or permanent loss is induced. Node 3 messages for this operation are finitely delayed; delayed follower writes complete at a fixed schedule point irrespective of commitment. Output separates queue construction, message publication, consumer effect and final storage state. The strict arm is a permitted control; the early arm deliberately explores the disputed caller duty, so neither arm creates property Evidence.

feedback.answered: README repeats same-batch concurrent send wording, but independently requires Entries before changed HardState. Ready.Messages remains stricter and raft.send explicitly describes append acknowledgments as persistence-dependent. Therefore a generic immediate-send scenario with a HardState update would not isolate the ambiguity. The selected experiment instead requires an unchanged follower HardState and produces every network response through the implementation.
remaining: Observe actual producer and consumer effects under the two explicit policies.
Contract applicability of the early-send arm remains unresolved; RawNode exploration does not establish Node permission or a consensus violation.
feedback.rationale: This small conditional experiment determines whether unchanged-HardState batches make the wording conflict consequential at the existing F-persistence-envelope consumer. If observed, retain the precise policy effect and then resolve or bound applicability rather than escalating it automatically to a safety finding.

input.question: With a real election/proposal/append prefix and unchanged follower HardState, does sending an actual synchronous follower Ready MsgAppResp before appending its same-batch entries cause leader Match and commit to advance while only the leader storage contains the operation, compared with persist-before-send?

result.summary: Prepared a validated two-policy exploration using actual election, append, and acknowledgment production. It compares persistence before reply against a conditional early-send policy; contract applicability remains unresolved, and no violation is claimed.

First, you must read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates
it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step
2.

1. Write HardState, Entries, and Snapshot to persistent storage if they are
not empty. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any
previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that
no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk,
and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while
entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an
optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its
followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type
MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be
large).

Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important that you
make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling.
The easiest way to achieve this is to serialize the messages directly inside
your main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine.
If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange()
to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point
by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange
(but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel
must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as
the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates.
This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed
in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an
implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage
type can be used for this (if you repopulate its state upon a
restart), or you can supply your own disk-backed implementation.

selections.rationale: Retain the initial source-grounded persistence and context handoffs while the required two-core-line overview remains incomplete. This is implementation understanding, not a formal Candidate or execution result.

feedback.answered: The inspected RawNode entry is explicitly thread-unsafe and sends Propose into raft.Step; a returned proposal call is not an observed commit or application. Followers forward only with a known leader and forwarding enabled; candidates reject proposals; leaders reject proposals during transfer or after losing their own Progress entry. appendEntry assigns current-term sequential indices, appends to the local log, and queues a self MsgAppResp through send. send queues MsgAppResp, MsgVoteResp and MsgPreVoteResp in msgsAfterAppend, including rejections. RawNode's synchronous path exposes remote replies under the Ready persistence contract and retains self replies for Advance. Its asynchronous path places queued replies in MsgStorageAppend.Responses. The Config interface requires reliable per-thread ordering and durable append writes before response delivery; these are caller duties, not effects proved by queue construction. Positive append responses update peer Progress before maybeCommit; the latter asks the tracker for an index and raftLog.maybeCommit additionally requires advancement and a matching nonzero current term. Step handles message terms before dispatch: ordinary lower-term replies exit without reaching the leader consumer; lower-term storage append responses do not stabilize entries but may complete a snapshot. reset discards votes, peer progress and readOnly tracking while retaining the log, and resets own Match to the local last index. Election vote handling checks vote eligibility and log freshness; candidate response handling distinguishes pre-vote from vote responses. These observations connect persistence support (A6) to formation (A1) and message-context filtering (A2), but do not yet establish the full backbone or a violation.
remaining: Read election production, leader initialization, timer and transfer paths, and the actual tracker/quorum implementations to explain authority acquisition and loss without assuming majority semantics.
Read configuration activation, restart construction, append conflict handling, snapshots, committed-entry application and public completion contracts to close the initial backbone.
Trace pendingReadIndexMessages separately from reset's readOnly replacement before characterizing old pending work across authority transitions.
Inspect the remainder of newStorageAppendRespMsg and its unstable-log consumer before selecting delayed storage completion as a focused discriminator.

No execution or safety conclusion is attributed to these source readings.

Existing term and entry-identity protections explain why stale storage completion is not generically safe to consume. No check has run and no correctness conclusion follows.

formation.explanation: RawNode.Propose or serialized Node loop enters the role-specific state machine. A leader admits entries, assigns term/index and appends locally; a follower forwards only with leader knowledge and enabled forwarding, while a candidate drops. Leader self support is queued, and follower MsgApp validates previous term and reconciles only an uncommitted suffix before queueing its response. send places append/vote responses behind persistence. Async MsgStorageAppend carries responses requiring ordered durable writes; synchronous Ready.Messages and Advance carry corresponding duties. Positive responses increase per-peer Match; configured majority order statistics (minimum of both groups for joint configuration) supply an index, and maybeCommit additionally matches the current term. Commit propagates through append and heartbeat; heartbeat commit is capped by recipient Match. Followers commit matching received prefixes and do not overwrite committed entries. Ready exposes committed entries, with async mode limited to stable local history and all modes pausing entries behind snapshots. The embedding state machine applies them in order, activates config entries, and correlates its own client completion. A successful proposal call has no commitment guarantee.

context.explanation: An election timeout or Campaign starts only for a locally eligible nonlearner without pending snapshot or unapplied committed configuration. Pre-vote leaves term/vote unchanged; real campaign increments term and queues its self vote until persistence. Voters check vote eligibility and last-log ordering; phase-specific replies are tallied once per sender over active voter sets. A won result establishes local leadership, resets replication tracking and appends an empty current-term entry. Higher-term traffic generally steps the node down, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; lower-term traffic is rejected before normal role consumers. CheckQuorum can remove leadership after insufficient recent voter activity. Transfer pauses proposals, catches up an eligible transferee, sends TimeoutNow, and aborts after an election timeout. Membership activation changes voter sets and local promotability; removal stepdown is configurable. Restart rebuilds from storage HardState and ConfState as follower. Snapshot restore accepts a newer committed prefix with recipient membership, either fast-forwarding a matching log or installing snapshot and reconstructed configuration.

connection.explanation: Authority reset clears tally, peer Match, and heartbeat read acknowledgments but preserves log and committed/application positions; old uncommitted entries can be replaced only above committed. Current-term entry commitment requalifies retained earlier log history. Configuration application changes eligibility of retained Progress, while new members start Match zero and joint votes/commits require both majorities. Queued persistence responses retain original RPC context: stale network replies cannot enter normal consumers, and stale append-thread entry acknowledgments cannot release unstable entries even if entry identities recur. A new-term HardState-only append can reconfirm in-progress history; snapshot and application completions remain term-independent because they concern committed state. Pending reads waiting for the first current-term commit survive reset, then receive a new commit index and new heartbeat acknowledgments in safe mode; already collected readOnly acknowledgments do not survive. ReadState is only a request-specific application-read prerequisite. Committed configuration application also governs campaign eligibility, and automatic joint exit follows applied progress.

After creating a Node, the user has a few responsibilities:

First, read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step 2.

1. Write Entries, HardState and Snapshot to persistent storage in order, i.e. Entries first, then HardState and Snapshot if they are not empty. If persistent storage supports atomic writes then all of them can be written together. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk, and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be large). Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important to make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling. The easiest way to achieve this is to serialise the messages directly inside the main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine. If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange() to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange (but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates. This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage type can be used for this (if repopulating its state upon a restart), or a custom disk-backed implementation can be supplied.

feedback.answered: The inspected RawNode entry is explicitly thread-unsafe and sends Propose into raft.Step; a returned proposal call is not an observed commit or application. Followers forward only with a known leader and forwarding enabled; candidates reject proposals; leaders reject proposals during transfer or after losing their own Progress entry. appendEntry assigns current-term sequential indices, appends to the local log, and queues a self MsgAppResp through send. send queues MsgAppResp, MsgVoteResp and MsgPreVoteResp in msgsAfterAppend, including rejections. RawNode's synchronous path exposes remote replies under the Ready persistence contract and retains self replies for Advance. Its asynchronous path places queued replies in MsgStorageAppend.Responses. The Config interface requires reliable per-thread ordering and durable append writes before response delivery; these are caller duties, not effects proved by queue construction. Positive append responses update peer Progress before maybeCommit; the latter asks the tracker for an index and raftLog.maybeCommit additionally requires advancement and a matching nonzero current term. Step handles message terms before dispatch: ordinary lower-term replies exit without reaching the leader consumer; lower-term storage append responses do not stabilize entries but may complete a snapshot. reset discards votes, peer progress and readOnly tracking while retaining the log, and resets own Match to the local last index. Election vote handling checks vote eligibility and log freshness; candidate response handling distinguishes pre-vote from vote responses. These observations connect persistence support (A6) to formation (A1) and message-context filtering (A2), but do not yet establish the full backbone or a violation.

formation.explanation: RawNode.Propose or serialized Node loop enters the role-specific state machine. A leader admits entries, assigns term/index and appends locally; a follower forwards only with leader knowledge and enabled forwarding, while a candidate drops. Leader self support is queued, and follower MsgApp validates previous term and reconciles only an uncommitted suffix before queueing its response. send places append/vote responses behind persistence. Async MsgStorageAppend carries responses requiring ordered durable writes; synchronous Ready.Messages and Advance carry corresponding duties. Positive responses increase per-peer Match; configured majority order statistics (minimum of both groups for joint configuration) supply an index, and maybeCommit additionally matches the current term. Commit propagates through append and heartbeat; heartbeat commit is capped by recipient Match. Followers commit matching received prefixes and do not overwrite committed entries. Ready exposes committed entries, with async mode limited to stable local history and all modes pausing entries behind snapshots. The embedding state machine applies them in order, activates config entries, and correlates its own client completion. A successful proposal call has no commitment guarantee.

context.explanation: An election timeout or Campaign starts only for a locally eligible nonlearner without pending snapshot or unapplied committed configuration. Pre-vote leaves term/vote unchanged; real campaign increments term and queues its self vote until persistence. Voters check vote eligibility and last-log ordering; phase-specific replies are tallied once per sender over active voter sets. A won result establishes local leadership, resets replication tracking and appends an empty current-term entry. Higher-term traffic generally steps the node down, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions; lower-term traffic is rejected before normal role consumers. CheckQuorum can remove leadership after insufficient recent voter activity. Transfer pauses proposals, catches up an eligible transferee, sends TimeoutNow, and aborts after an election timeout. Membership activation changes voter sets and local promotability; removal stepdown is configurable. Restart rebuilds from storage HardState and ConfState as follower. Snapshot restore accepts a newer committed prefix with recipient membership, either fast-forwarding a matching log or installing snapshot and reconstructed configuration.

connection.explanation: Authority reset clears tally, peer Match, and heartbeat read acknowledgments but preserves log and committed/application positions; old uncommitted entries can be replaced only above committed. Current-term entry commitment requalifies retained earlier log history. Configuration application changes eligibility of retained Progress, while new members start Match zero and joint votes/commits require both majorities. Queued persistence responses retain original RPC context: stale network replies cannot enter normal consumers, and stale append-thread entry acknowledgments cannot release unstable entries even if entry identities recur. A new-term HardState-only append can reconfirm in-progress history; snapshot and application completions remain term-independent because they concern committed state. Pending reads waiting for the first current-term commit survive reset, then receive a new commit index and new heartbeat acknowledgments in safe mode; already collected readOnly acknowledgments do not survive. ReadState is only a request-specific application-read prerequisite. Committed configuration application also governs campaign eligibility, and automatic joint exit follows applied progress.

MemoryStorage substitutes for disk durability and no crash or permanent loss is induced.
